role: Shared UI-test harness for the whole EmuquUITests target (timing scale, English launch args, accessibility-identifier constants, element lookup, tab/More navigation, first-run gate walking) plus the EmuquUITests smoke suite (tabs, dashboard, record, settings, history, paywall, disclaimer, Flo) and UITestTimingTests pinning the timing scale.
types: UITestTiming: enum — global wait multiplier (scale=2) and s() to widen deadlines
UITestLanguage: enum — launch args forcing en/en_US
UITestID: enum — string constants mirroring app .accessibilityIdentifier values and tab titles
UITestFind: enum — element lookup/tap helpers tolerant of SwiftUI identifier forwarding
UITestNav: enum — tab selection and More/Dashboard navigation with retries
UITestLaunch: enum (+ extension) — walks disclaimer/onboarding/paywall gates; background-to-persist
EmuquUITests: class — XCTestCase smoke suite of main flows
toplevel: Static constant tables only: UITestID identifiers (all verified to appear as string literals in Emuqu/ sources), tab titles (tabCoachTitle='Flo'), gate lists in UITestLaunch, and EmuquUITests tab tables. UITestTiming.scale is a hardcoded 2 (comment lines 16-24 explains env var TEST_RUNNER_UITEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE did not reach the runner).

flags.text: Passes the bare '-UITests' launch argument, which no production code reads (only -UITests-FreshInstall at AppLaunchRecovery.swift:185 and -UITests-ForcePaywall/-UITests-SeedArchive at UITestLaunchArguments.swift:18,23 are checked); it is inert
UITestFind doc comment at lines 201-213 describes an `onScreen` helper using debugDescription but is orphaned above isSafelyHittable's doc; onScreen itself is at line 274 with no doc. Cosmetic only.

UITestID constants moreAbout, paywallTermsOfUse, settingsMetricGuide, settingsMethodology, settingsTermsOfUse, settingsRoutes, settingsTags and settingsPermissions are referenced by no test in EmuquUITests (grep UITestID.<name>)

flags.text: Two harness comments contradict each other about isHittable under a fullScreenCover: 228-235 says isHittable is the only thing that knows a cover sits on the tab bar, 681-684 says on iOS 26 the tab bar under a fullScreenCover reports hittable. toMainUI's final readiness poll (642-645) and OnboardingFlowUITests' 'tabs must not be tappable' assertion both rely on the first claim; if the second is true, toMainUI's true does not prove no cover is up and the onboarding assertion fails on iOS 26

branches.effect: return false; otherwise coordinate tap and return true

flags.text: A coordinate tap on an element covered by a sheet is delivered to the cover and still returns true, so callers that use the result as 'tapped' (e.g. EmuquUITests.swift:1276) cannot tell a swallowed tap from a real one

flags.text: No app-frame intersection check: a frame laid out below the window gets a tap off-screen that reports true; acceptAssistantDisclaimer documents exactly this failure and works around it by swiping first
